THR the National Pavilion format of the Venice Biennale, in favor of a borderless, theme-based exhibition model.
The Venice Biennale is one of the world's oldest and most prestigious art exhibitions, traditionally organized around National Pavilions where individual countries select artists to represent their national identity and cultural output.
A borderless, theme-based model would abolish these state-sponsored boundaries, instead organizing the entire festival around curated global concepts (e.g., "The Post-Human Condition") where artists are selected and grouped based on their work's relevance to the theme rather than their country of origin.

entry.Resolution:
THP the response by PAFA to the response by Seattle.
In late 2017, during the “me too era”, it was revealed that Chuck Close, a highly influential and stylistically renowned American painter, had sexually assaulted and harassed several women. At the time, Close had been lending many of his portraits to Pennsylvania Academy of the Fine Arts (PAFA) and Seattle University free of charge. PAFA chose to keep their Close exhibition displayed, adding placards explaining and condemning his behaviour, and creating a space where visitors could write their thoughts about issues of gender and accountability in the arts. They also organised an exhibition by female artists to sit alongside Close’s work. PAFA continues to teach Close’s work in its curriculum. Conversely, Seattle responded by removing Close’s exhibition and no longer teaching or displaying his work.

entry.Topic Committee: Ethan Bordoff, Jane Kelly, Dari Zell, Andy Montvelisky, Anika (equity)

entry.Resolution:

They carry out interventions where they take elements from everyday space (walls, sidewalks, lampposts, bridges, etc.) modifying them in different ways. For the purposes of this debate, two trends can be delimited: a) Celebratory interventions: Their premise is the recovery of joy through motivating phrases and very bright colors (eg Yarn-bombing, painting buses using elements of pop culture, remodeling facades, etc. ) b) Uncomfortable interventions: They have as a premise the questioning of canonical values through political slogans and images against institutions or structural problems (eg, graffiti with ridicule of politics, crude images, etc.)

entry.Resolution:
THP the UK system to the US for college admissions.
The UK system only allows applicants to apply to five schools. Admissions are primarily based on grades and test scores, with circumstances and written materials considered secondary. If students do not receive an admission offer by summer, a ‘clearing’ period starts where students can reapply to schools with open seats still available. Students must also apply directly to a major.
The US system has no limit to the number of schools students can apply to. Admissions are ‘holistic’, considering extracurriculars, essays, grades, and test scores, as well as circumstances in the application process. In addition, there are decision rounds, where students can apply early to schools. These sometimes include binding agreements, where students must attend the university if admitted.

entry.Resolution:
THBT the Sri Lankan government should aggressively provide financial incentives for high performing school graduates to enter less lucrative fields for their university education.

Medicine, Engineering and Law are the most commonly selected degrees by high-ranking entrants, due to their high pay and/or associated social standing. As a consequence of this social norm, many less lucrative fields and occupations such as teaching, agriculture, scientific research, environmental conservation, social sciences etc. have lagged behind in their advancement, since most highly educated graduates opt into mainstream jobs.

Athletes compete in interscholastic leagues and, at the tertiary level, through the NCAA (National Collegiate Athletic Association), which offers athletic scholarships. Young athletes are typically drafted after graduation and sign professional contracts with teams. The European model develops athletes primarily through sports clubs where players are recruited young, trained by professional volunteers, and may be promoted based on sporting merit, which may result in signing professional contracts in their teens. Young players are typically amateurs and from the grassroots, and training is largely separate from formal education.

It provides a commitment to collective defense ("an attack on one is an attack on all") without imposing a mandatory, automatic, or predetermined military response. Adding automaticity would require NATO members to provide immediate military assistance if any member is attacked.

Under this view, wars may appear to be ethnically motivated, but likely because leaders of insurgent groups stoke ethnic conflict in order to gain support for their side.

Qualified double jeopardy allows the same government to try them again if there was either 1) a serious legal error or 2) substantial new evidence is discovered.
If someone is found guilty and later discovers new evidence proving their innocence, seeking a new trial is generally not considered double jeopardy, but rather a request for post-conviction relief (like a direct appeal or writ of habeas corpus).

PFMCs were generally operated on donations and volunteers. PFMCs were harassed by city health inspectors, local police, and the FBI. Utilitarianism evaluates actions based on their consequences, aiming to maximize overall well-being. AGI is an AI that matches or surpasses human capabilities across virtually all cognitive tasks.

entry.Resolution:
This House believes in Robert Nozick’s Entitlement Theory of Property.
INFOSLIDE: Nozick’s theory posits that a person may justly own a piece of property if and only if (1) that property was justly acquired by its initial owner; (2) it passed on to the current owner through a chain of voluntary exchanges or gifts; (3) any violation of the first two conditions was rectified by just compensation.

entry.Resolution:
THR the popularization of RCTs in developmental economics research.
Randomized controlled trials are experiments that apply an intervention to only a randomly selected portion of the target population, so that you can compare the effects of the intervention against a group that didn’t receive it. Since the popularization of RCTs, the field of development economics has shifted from a focus largely on nation-scale problems with no clear answers (like why countries are poor), to a focus largely on smaller problems that can be definitively answered (like whether investing in digital learning solutions in schools outperforms traditional investments).
entry.Name: NYPDL
entry.Topic Committee: Ethan Bordoff, Dari Zell, Andy Montvelisky

entry.Resolution: THP economics to be seen as a political field rather than a scientific field.

entry.Resolution: THR the increasing privatisation of the space industry.

entry.Resolution:
In places with high levels of religious radicalism, THBT schools should push progressive interpretations of religious texts as opposed to secular classes on ethics and morality.
Religious radicalism involves literalist, often extreme interpretations of faith for the purpose of enforcing religious law.
entry.Name: NYPDL
entry.Topic Committee: Ethan Bordoff, Dari Zell, Andy Montvelisky

entry.Resolution:
THP a world where people who care about creating change in the world primarily follow the 'earn to give model' instead of 'working to maximize social good'.
The "earn-to-give model" is a philosophy/movement that suggests the best strategy for people who want to create a change in the world is to earn a substantial income and then donate a significant portion of it to cost- effective charities. On the other hand, "work that maximizes social good" focuses on how you can create a positive impact on people through your work in various ways, such as social entrepreneurship or working in non-profit organizations. Usually, those working to maximize social good choose sectors that are less profitable and earn less money than the earn-to-give model.
entry.Name: NYPDL
entry.Topic Committee: Ethan Bordoff, Dari Zell, Andy Montvelisky

entry.Resolution:
THW establish life on the paradise planet.
You and a group of scientists are sent into outer space on a sub-light speed ship for the mission to resettle Earth after the effects of climate change subsides. Some humans remained on Earth, and while human societies survived, civilization did not, returning human activity on Earth to a primitive state. While waiting for climate change to expire, you have ventured around the galaxy and found an uninhabited paradise planet that seems better able to provide for society than earth. Due to the nature of sub-light-speed travel, your crew only aged a few years even though a millennia passed on Earth (and all of your commanders have died). You now have two exclusive choices; to return to Earth and fulfill your mission or to abandon your mission and establish life on the paradise planet.
entry.Name: NYPDL
entry.Topic Committee: Ethan Bordoff, Dari Zell, Andy Montvelisky

entry.Resolution:
THR the decline of the humanities in higher education.
In academic settings, “the humanities” is contrasted with the study of natural sciences, social sciences, and professional training. Core fields in the humanities include: literature, philosophy, history, religion, art.
entry.Name: NYPDL
entry.Topic Committee: Ethan Bordoff, Dari Zell, Andy Montvelisky

entry.Resolution:
THW mandate all scientists to periodically conduct reproducibility research. (e.g. reproducing the result of existing research or experiments meta-analysis of reproducibility of pre-existing experiments)
Reproducibility is a major principle of the scientific method. It means when different researchers follow the same methodology of a research (i.e. experiments or observational study) to reproduce the result it should match the result of the original research. Currently many research results in some fields are said to be unreproducible especially in several branches of Biology Psychology and Behavioral Economics etc.
entry.Name: NYPDL
entry.Topic Committee: Ethan Bordoff, Dari Zell, Andy Montvelisky

entry.Resolution:
THS the rise of Sci-Hub.
Sci-Hub is a website that provides free access to millions of paywalled and open-access research papers and books. Sci-Hub obtains paywalled papers by presenting compromised university usernames and passwords to the publishers' websites via the universities' proxy websites. The means by which Sci-Hub obtains usernames and passwords are legal and illegal.
entry.Name: NYPDL
entry.Topic Committee: Ethan Bordoff, Dari Zell, Andy Montvelisky

entry.Resolution: TH, as a prominent progressive journalist in an authoritarian state, W shift their efforts on informal journalism (e.g., citizen journalism, hyper-local reporting) as opposed to working within large traditional media agencies.

entry.Resolution: In developed countries, THP fierce polarization over widespread political apathy.

entry.Topic Committee: Ethan Bordoff, Dari Zell, Andy Montvelisky

entry.Resolution:
Assuming feasibility, THP a world with the TrustHuman system.
In the TrustHuman system, people can submit a numerical review of their interactions with others. Every person then has a personal, with a weighted system where long-term interactions are weighed more than short-term interactions (e.g. a review from one's long term partner would have a larger effect than a review from a waiter in a restaurant one has visited once). People are allowed to change their rating of others if circumstances change, and you can only rate people you have personally interacted with. Everyone's overall rating is publicly accessible, but one cannot access each individual rating. Each person's rating is only accessible once there is a sufficient number of reviews.
entry.Name: NYPDL
entry.Topic Committee: Ethan Bordoff, Dari Zell, Andy Montvelisky

entry.Resolution:
THR the Goldwater Rule.
Since 1973, the American Psychiatric Association’s Goldwater Rule has instructed psychiatrists not to speculate on the mental health of public figures whom they have not examined. The Rule is widely-followed, and similar norms exist among other mental health professionals.
entry.Name: NYPDL
entry.Topic Committee: Ethan Bordoff, Dari Zell, Andy Montvelisky

entry.Resolution:
THBT the feminist movement should actively frame consumers of the manosphere as victims rather than ideological opponents.
The manosphere is a loose network of online communities, blogs, and influencers centered on men’s issues, often promoting masculinity and traditional gender roles to an extreme degree.
entry.Name: NYPDL
entry.Topic Committee: Ethan Bordoff, Dari Zell, Andy Montvelisky

entry.Resolution: THBT the response to global pandemics should be led by the World Health Organization rather than by individual governments.

entry.Resolution:
Assuming the US successfully invades Greenland without casualties on either side, TH, as the EU, W choose a passive response rather than an aggressive response.
An aggressive response to an invasion includes enacting sweeping sanctions, expelling diplomats, military action and abandoning bi- and multilateral collaboration. A passive response to an invasion may instead include seeking agreement through negotiations and mediation.
entry.Name: NYPDL
entry.Topic Committee: Ethan Bordoff, Dari Zell, Andy Montvelisky

entry.Resolution:
THP a widespread adoption of process-based as opposed to outcomes-based environmental regulation.
Process-based environmental regulations refers to regulations that prescribe specific practices (i.e. use of renewable energy sources, specific farming techniques to reduce emission, etc.) in protecting the environment. In comparison, outcomes-based regulation (e.g. emission caps or waste reduction goals) without prescribing how they must be achieved.
entry.Name: NYPDL

entry.Resolution: THP art that addresses class inequality through the glorification of working-class lives (e.g. Paterson, Empire of Light, American Beauty, Take Me Home, Country Roads) over art that addresses class inequality through the demonisation of economic elites (e.g. The Wolf of Wall Street, The Great Gatsby, Snowpiercer, American Psycho).

entry.Resolution:
THO the trend of prioritising technical elements over program components in figure skating scoring.
The ISU (Ice Skating Union) recently changed its judging system. The new system rewards skaters for performing technical elements (complicated jumps or turns, etc...) over program elements (artistic expression), The move was intended to make the sport more objective and offer more transparency in how skaters are judged.
entry.Name: NYPDL

On Tuesday, OpenAI shut down its video creation platform Sora, claiming it was a “distraction” from focusing on corporate products such as software generation tools.
THO the increasing trend of AI companies shifting focus from consumer-facing products to corporate clients.

entry.Resolution:
THW join the protests.
You are a progressive, only child of a wealthy political dynasty, who recently graduated from university and are expected to inherit your family’s power. A large corruption scandal has emerged around infrastructure projects linked to your relatives. Despite growing public outrage and investigations, your family has denied all allegations, refused cooperation, and is likely to get away with it. Your attempts to persuade them to cooperate have failed. Inside the household, relatives insist on denying the allegations and waiting for the controversy to pass. You are expected to stay quiet and protect your eventual succession, with the understanding that you could set a different course once you are in charge. At the same time, protests continue to grow, creating the possibility of distancing yourself from your family now and building legitimacy as their eventual successor.
entry.Name: NYPDL
entry.Topic Committee: Ethan Bordoff, Dari Zell, Andy Montvelisky

entry.Resolution:
TH, as the young alien superhuman, W choose option B over option A.
You are a young alien superhuman living on Earth. You were raised by a kind and grounded human family who taught you the value of humility, everyday life, and trust in human systems. You’ve grown up believing in the importance of restraint : that your powers should be used only when absolutely necessary, and always within the boundaries of law and society. Recently, you’ve discovered messages left by your biological alien father. He believes that Earth is unstable and that your superior abilities give you a duty to rise above others to guide, protect, and shape civilization. He urges you to embrace your potential by taking leadership and shaping the world around you. You now have two options: Option A, where you continue to live as a normal human who occasionally uses your powers to help others, or Option B, whereby you attempt to take a major proactive role in reshaping and altering existing power structures.
entry.Name: NYPDL
entry.Topic Committee: Ethan Bordoff, Dari Zell, Andy Montvelisky

entry.Resolution:
TH, as the engineer, W choose to destroy the machine.
You are an engineer living in a liberal democracy. Your corporation has secretly developed a machine that can predict the future of all newborn children, such as whether or not the child grows up to be a serial killer or a doctor who can cure cancer. The machine’s predictions so far have never failed, despite hundreds of tests. The government gets wind of this invention and compels you to hand over this machine.

THBT developing countries should impose windfall taxes.
A windfall tax is imposed on companies or businesses that achieve excessive profit during unforeseen events such as favorable market conditions, resource discoveries, or regulatory changes; e.g. global surge of oil prices, discovery of new medicines during a disease outbreak, etc.

entry.Resolution:
Assuming feasibility, THS the implementation of a financial transaction tax.
A financial transaction tax is a tax on purchasing assets (e.g. stock sales, currencies, derivatives), which seeks to “throw sand in the wheels” of financial markets by discouraging trading for short term gains and reducing the use of financial resources for speculative use.

As a result, live performances have become an increasingly important source of income for many musicians."

THO the rise of cinematic universes in the film industry.

entry.Resolution:
THS the political ideology of pragmatism.
Pragmatism is a political ideology that promotes a flexible, anti-ideological approach to governance based on "what works", focused on achieving results over adherence to a particular set of values or beliefs.

entry.Resolution:
TH, as a Republican candidate for Congress in a competitive race in an upper-middle class swing district, W choose to run on a neoconservative policy platform rather than a populist policy platform.
A "neoconservative policy platform" refers to a set of policies that advocate for free trade, the promotion of democracy, and American military interventions overseas, alongside support for free-market economics and socially conservative values. On the other hand, a "populist policy platform" favours protectionist trade policies, opposes the promotion of democracy, immigration, and military involvement abroad, while still endorsing social conservatism and some free market economic policies. A "swing district" refers to a U.S. Congressional district known for frequently changing party control and regularly having closely contested elections.
entry.Name: NYPDL
entry.Topic Committee: Ethan Bordoff,  Jane Kelly, Andy Montvelisky, Arnob Mitra (equity)

entry.Resolution: THBT North American cities with declining populations should embrace a policy of "de-growth" (e.g. repurposing unused infrastructure for other uses, converting unused parking lots to parks) that seeks to maximize quality of life for the remaining residents rather than trying to encourage growth (e.g. offering tax breaks to businesses that move to the city).
entry.Name: NYPDL
entry.Topic Committee: Ethan Bordoff,  Jane Kelly, Andy Montvelisky, Arnob Mitra (equity)

entry.Resolution:
THR the dominance of single-use zoning in American cities.
Single-use zoning is an urban planning system in which specific areas of a city are designated for only one type of activity, such as residential, commercial, or industrial use. This separation restricts the mixing of functions within the same neighbourhood, leading to distinct zones for living, working, and shopping.
entry.Name: NYPDL
entry.Topic Committee: Ethan Bordoff,  Jane Kelly, Andy Montvelisky, Arnob Mitra (equity)

entry.Resolution:
THS the widespread implementation of odious debt doctrines.
“Odious debt” is a hypothetical legal doctrine holding that a new government need not honor sovereign debt obligations if the debt was incurred without the people's consent, did not benefit the people, and the lenders knew or should have known this.
entry.Name: NYPDL
entry.Topic Committee: Ethan Bordoff,  Jane Kelly, Andy Montvelisky, Arnob Mitra (equity)

entry.Resolution:
THP social movements that frame justice as having instrumental value, rather than intrinsic value.
Things are deemed to have instrumental value if they help one achieve a particular end; intrinsic values, by contrast, are understood to be desirable in and of themselves.
entry.Name: NYPDL
entry.Topic Committee: Ethan Bordoff,  Jane Kelly, Andy Montvelisky, Arnob Mitra (equity)

entry.Resolution:
THO academic activism.
Academic activism refers to a phenomenon where academics take an explicitly political standpoint in their work and outside it with the aim of bringing about social change. Activist academics openly associate with different social and political groups or movements. Examples include Judith Butler (American philosopher and gender theorist, and active in the Occupy movement), Taimur Rahman (Professor at the Lahore University of Management Sciences, and Secretary-General of the Mazdoor Kisan Party (communist political party).
entry.Name: NYPDL
entry.Topic Committee: Ethan Bordoff,  Jane Kelly, Andy Montvelisky, Arnob Mitra (equity)

entry.Resolution:
THR the rise of international adoption.
In recent years in Western liberal democracies, there has been a trend of adopting from abroad, largely from developing countries.
entry.Name: NYPDL
entry.Topic Committee: Ethan Bordoff,  Jane Kelly, Andy Montvelisky, Arnob Mitra (equity)

entry.Resolution: In case of a zombie-epidemic, THBT zombies have a right to a humane life in special zombie-habitats.
entry.Name: NYPDL
entry.Topic Committee: Ethan Bordoff,  Jane Kelly, Andy Montvelisky, Arnob Mitra (equity)

entry.Resolution:
THBT governments should introduce the “Zombie Voting System” for firms that receive significant assistance during financial crises.
The details of a proposed “Zombie Voting System” are as follows. As the recovery from an economic crisis begins, workers at firms that received significant financial assistance from the government during the crisis would vote for one of two options: 1. Vote to immediately liquidate the firm they work at, and receive unemployment benefits for longer OR 2. Vote not to liquidate, and the government would inject some more cash to make the company viable and help pay off its remaining debts. But if it subsequently were to fail (go bankrupt), the workers’ unemployment coverage would be severely curtailed. The choice of option would be determined by a simple majority vote, with all current workers entitled to one vote.
entry.Name: NYPDL
entry.Topic Committee: Ethan Bordoff,  Jane Kelly, Andy Montvelisky, Arnob Mitra (equity)

entry.Resolution:
Assuming feasibility of reaching a quarantine zone, THW rather live in a quarantine zone than be a survivalist.
10 years after a zombie infection broke out, world governments have collapsed and hordes of zombies roam the planet. Human civilisation is largely confined to quarantine zones under martial law by ruthless authoritarian regimes. You are a reclusive survivalist living in a remote town all alone after it was evacuated prior to the Zombie horde's arrival. You are resourceful and the town is well defended by barricades on all sides.
entry.Name: NYPDL
entry.Topic Committee: Ethan Bordoff,  Jane Kelly, Andy Montvelisky, Arnob Mitra (equity)

entry.Resolution:
THBT nation-building efforts in postcolonial states should focus on unifying people through appeals to universal humanism, as opposed to focusing on the evils of colonialism.
Leaders like Aimé Césaire and Steve Biko in post-apartheid South Africa emphasized reconciliation and the notion of a "Rainbow Nation" rooted in universal human rights and dignity.
After Zimbabwe’s independence in 1980, its rulers heavily emphasized the ongoing evils of colonialism and white minority rule as the central narrative of nation-building. Political messaging frequently framed contemporary political conflicts as a continuation of the anti-colonial struggle.
entry.Name: NYPDL
entry.Topic Committee: Ethan Bordoff,  Jane Kelly, Andy Montvelisky, Arnob Mitra (equity)

entry.Resolution:
TH, as China, W prioritize future investments in agriculture (e.g., irrigation, R&D, mechanization and other inputs like fertilizer) over investments in infrastructure and manufacturing across sub-Saharan Africa.
Since 2000, China has committed $160 billion in loans (often at favorable terms) to African economic development, focused on infrastructure projects (such as Kenya’s Standard Gauge Railway, built with the help of a $3.2 billion loan). In addition, it has become a major trading partner of many countries across Africa, being the largest source of imports in South Africa, Egypt, Madagascar, Sudan, Kenya, and Tanzania, among others.
entry.Name: NYPDL
entry.Topic Committee: Ethan Bordoff,  Jane Kelly, Andy Montvelisky, Arnob Mitra (equity)

entry.Resolution:
THBT legal systems should have the option of private prosecution, similarly to South Africa.
Under South African law, private actors may seek permission from the National Prosecution Authority (NPA) to privately prosecute people for criminal offences which the NPA is either unable or unwilling to pursue. A refusal by the NPA to allow private prosecution, without a valid reason, may be challenged in court. If the private actor’s prosecution fails, they must cover the legal costs of the defendant. The NPA retains oversight over all privately-prosecuted cases and can step in or stop them at any time, though these actions can be challenged in court if found to be unreasonable or politically-motivated.
entry.Name: NYPDL
entry.Topic Committee: Ethan Bordoff,  Jane Kelly, Andy Montvelisky, Arnob Mitra (equity)

entry.Resolution:
In high crime areas, THBT prosecutors should focus on litigating "Al Capone" cases as opposed to trying violent or drug cases.
For the purposes of this debate, "Al Capone" cases involve pursuing organized crime for financial crimes (e.g. laundering, tax evasion, fraud) rather than through conviction on violent or drug crime.
entry.Name: NYPDL
entry.Topic Committee: Ethan Bordoff,  Jane Kelly, Andy Montvelisky, Arnob Mitra (equity)

entry.Resolution:
THP a multipolar world order to a bipolar one.

Doctors believed that without separation, both girls would die within the first five years of their lives because of the strain on Jodie’s heart. However, if they were separated, Mary would certainly die, while Jodie had a strong chance of living a relatively normal life. The operation needed to be done shortly after birth, or it would have become virtually impossible. The parents, devout Catholics, refused consent for the surgery. The hospital sought court permission to proceed. The case went to the Court of Appeal, which ruled that the operation was lawful. The surgery went ahead, Mary died shortly after, and Jodie survived.

The soul is now intrinsically flawed but capable of redemption through good practices and the benevolent intervention of God. Patan tempts humans toward sin but doesn’t have anything close to the power of God. The second is that there are two opposed gods of roughly equal power (we’ll call them God and Patan [pah-TAHN]), and that human creation is a byproduct of the battle between good and evil. The choices that humans ultimately make sway the outcome of the battle between God and Patan in the long term.

entry.Resolution:
THP a conquistadorial to a liberationist interpretation of Minecraft's gameplay in the cultural zeitgeist.
The conquistadorial interpretation of gameplay is an analytical framework in which a player’s primary actions (such as exploration, resource extraction, territorial expansion, and the defeat of major entities) are understood principally as acts of domination and control over a virtual world. Under this interpretation, progression is driven by the accumulation of success and the mastery of personal skill, rather than by immediate needs of survival or coexistence. The liberationist interpretation of gameplay understands a player’s actions as primarily oriented toward emancipation, protection, or restoration. This includes defending vulnerable groups, eliminating hostile threats, or restoring balance within the game world. This interpretation frames progression as morally justified through the removal of obstacles that constrain the freedom, safety, or autonomy of oneself or other friendly entities.

Wicked is a musical that reimagines the world of The Wizard of Oz by centering the story on Elphaba, later labeled the Wicked Witch of the West, and Glinda, who becomes the Good Witch. In Oz, political power is consolidated under the Wizard, who sustains his rule through propaganda, public spectacle, and the systematic scapegoating of Elphaba, while also repressing Animals who are capable of speech and independent thought. Glinda rises to prominence by aligning herself with the Wizard, gaining popularity, legitimacy, and close access to power as a symbol of goodness and stability. Although Glinda privately disagrees with many of the Wizard's actions, she chooses to remain within the system, believing that gradual reform and quiet influence are preferable to open confrontation that might destabilize Oz. Elphaba, by contrast, rejects the Wizard's legitimacy and engages in direct resistance, positioning herself as a radical challenger to the existing order and enabling the state to frame her dissent as villainy, resulting in her public vilification, isolation, and persecution even as her opposition exposes the regime's underlying injustices.

In Star Wars, certain individuals are born with the power to access the 'Force' -- an energy field that binds the universe together. A Force-sensitive individual can levitate objects, trick minds, and sometimes predict the short-term future. The Jedi believe that the best way to control the Force is by suppressing your emotions, and so follow a philosophy of detachment from the living world (including rejecting attachments such as romantic relationships). The Sith believe in encouraging strong emotion and using it to fuel the Force. Both seek peace in the galaxy.

The 7 nanometre process refers to the ability to manufacture semiconductor technology that is 7nm in size. Huawei's latest smartphone is reported to include 7nm process semiconductors. If true, this would prove China's ability to independently develop this technology, despite sanctions from the United States to prevent China from doing so. Currently, only South Korea and Taiwan can develop semiconductors smaller than 7nm to commercial scale. Semiconductors are a critical part of modern electronics (e.g computers, smartphones etc).

entry.Resolution:
THP the carbon tax system to the carbon cap-and-trade system.
A carbon tax is a fixed fee imposed on carbon emissions, providing a direct financial incentive for businesses to reduce their carbon footprint. In contrast, a cap-and-trade system sets a maximum limit (cap) on total emissions and allows companies to buy, sell, or trade emission permits, creating a market-driven approach to reducing pollution.

entry.Resolution:
For health care emergencies requiring collective action (e.g. pandemics, pollution-related illness, etc.), THW grant the WHO the ability to implement international laws that override sovereign laws.
The World Health Organization (WHO) is a specialized agency of the United Nations responsible for international public health. Its mission is to promote health, respond to global health emergencies, and address major health challenges. The WHO provides guidelines, research, and technical support to help countries strengthen their health systems. Currently, the WHO has no enforcement powers and relies on countries voluntarily following its recommendations.

entry.Resolution:
THS green central banking.
Green central banking refers to central banks deliberately using their monetary policy instruments to incentivize climate-friendly market activities. For instance, targeted green lending programmes, targeted green bond purchase programmes, ""brown penalties"" (higher interest rates for pollution-intensive banks or businesses), lowering the financing rate for banks that offer collateral with a smaller carbon footprint, and mandatory disclosures of climate risks. For the purposes of the debate, green central banking would support climate-friendly policies at the expense of traditional monetary objectives such as targeting inflation rates, ensuring financial stability and market efficiency, as well as retaining neutrality of intervention.

entry.Resolution:
THBT the US should curb the rapid growth of data centers.
Data centers are crucial physical infrastructures which stores large amounts of digital information that fuel emerging technologies such as AI and the Internet of Things. Currently, there are over 5000 data centers across the United States which are primarily developed for Big Tech companies like Google, Meta, Microsoft and Amazon. While data centers have brought billions of dollars in investments and created thousands of jobs, they are extremely energy-intensive and use immense amounts of local resources especially water.

entry.Resolution:
THP the legislative review model to the judicial supremacy model in liberal democracies.
Constitutional review is the set of legal mechanisms used to verify whether laws, normative acts, or decisions of public authorities comply with a country's Constitution. There are two institutional models widely adopted by liberal democracies: (i) In the legislative override model, parliament can, through a formal process typically requiring a qualified majority such as two-thirds of votes, declare that a certain law will remain valid even after having been deemed unconstitutional by a court. This decision must be renewed periodically or is suspended. An example of this model is Canada, which adopts this approach through the so-called "notwithstanding clause" (Section 33 of the Charter of Rights and Freedoms). (ii) In the judicial supremacy model, decisions issued by constitutional courts, especially supreme courts, are final in constitutional matters. The Legislature can respond politically, such as by approving constitutional amendments or altering ordinary laws, but does not possess formal mechanisms to directly nullify these decisions. This model is characteristic of the United States, where only a new decision by the Supreme Court can modify an interpretation previously established by the Court.

Individuals displaced by climate change (climate migrants) lack formal recognition as "refugees" under the 1951 Convention, often leaving them in a legal void regarding cross-border protections.

Developing countries typically issue licenses to allow certain companies to extract resources from public lands. After a license is issued, there are two potential ways for governments to make money off of revenue extraction. The first is Resource Profit Taxes, where countries tax the profits made from resource extraction at a significantly higher rate than regular taxes on corporate profit (relative to other countries). The second is Resource Royalties, where countries sell the rights to extract resources to a company for a fixed fee (either per area or per unit mined).

entry.Resolution:
THP metaphorical art over visceral art as a tool for social change.
Metaphorical art uses symbolism, abstraction, or participatory elements to communicate political or social critique indirectly. An example of metaphorical art is Untitled (Portrait of Ross in L.A.), created by Felix Gonzalez-Torres during the AIDS epidemic. The work consists of a pile of colorful, individually wrapped candies weighing 175 pounds—the weight of Gonzalez-Torres’ partner, Ross, before he contracted AIDS. Visitors are encouraged to take pieces of candy, and as the pile diminishes, it mirrors Ross’s physical decline due to the illness. [image of Untitled]
Visceral art confronts viewers with graphic, emotionally intense imagery to provoke an immediate reaction. An example of visceral art is The Third of May 1808 by Francisco Goya. The painting depicts the execution of Spanish civilians by French soldiers during the Peninsular War. Goya presents the violence directly: armed soldiers, terrified civilians, and the immediacy of death. [image of The Third of May 1808]

entry.Resolution:
THP art without closure in transitional justice eras, as opposed to art that offers closure.
Transitional justice eras refer to specific historical and political moments in which a society is reckoning with a legacy of mass injustice, violence, or authoritarian rule—often following dictatorships, civil wars, state-sponsored repression, or colonial regimes. These periods, occurring during or shortly after political transition, are characterized by the involvement of processes such as truth commissions, war crimes trials, reparations for victims, memorialization through museums or art, and institutional reform (e.g., judiciary, police, or military). Art that offers no closure seeks to reflect the unresolved, complex, and emotionally ambiguous terrain of a society still grappling with its past. These works often reject neat moral binaries or redemptive arcs. Art that offers closure on the other hand, aims to heal, redeem, or resolve historical trauma, often providing a sense of catharsis, or restored moral order.

entry.Resolution:
THP the ADPA model of debate to the BP model of debate.
British Parliamentary (BP) debate and American Parliamentary Debate (APDA) are the two premier parliamentary debate (“Parli”) styles at the college level. Although both styles have some similarities (there is the Government side and an Opposition side), there are three major distinctions between each style’s model of debate. First, BP debates consist of four teams, each with two debaters: Opening Government (OG), Opening Opposition (OO), Closing Government (CG), and Closing Opposition (CO). Each speaker on a team has one speech, which is 7 minutes long. The order is as following: OG, OO, OG, OO, CG, CO, CG, CO. The winner of the debate is not determined by which side wins, but by a ranked placement of all four teams from first to fourth based on their individual contributions to the round. By contrast, APDA utilizes a two-versus-two format with alternating Government and Opposition speeches (Prime Minister 7 min, Leader of Opposition 8 min, etc.) similar to the NYPDL. Second, APDA debates allow teams to run pre-prepared affirmative cases, with Government teams preparing cases/motions in advance of the round and then presenting them to the Opposition side, who has 15 minutes to prepare for them. These must give the Opposition side sufficient ground, or else the Opposition side can “tight call” the case and explain why it is skewed. In contrast, BP motions are announced shortly before the debate, and teams construct arguments extemporaneously with 15 minutes of preparation time. Third, judges in BP are explicitly instructed to prioritize “truth over tech,” meaning they should evaluate arguments based on their plausibility, comparative reasoning, and real-world logic, rather than technical concessions or dropped arguments. APDA judging is generally more flow-oriented, placing greater emphasis on technical execution, extensions, and strategic drops.

entry.Resolution:
THR the rise of paraphrase theory in Public Forum debate.
Public Forum (PF) is a two-versus-two debate format in which each partner delivers two speeches. The speeches alternate between the affirmative (pro) and negative (con) sides on a monthly “resolution” published by the National Speech & Debate Association (NSDA). These resolutions address contemporary issues, such as “NATO should increase defense commitments to the Baltic states.” Because of this structure, PF requires extensive research and collection of evidence, with debaters writing and researching arguments for the resolution over the course of the month. At most local tournaments, debaters paraphrase their evidence in speeches rather than reading it verbatim. However, many teams competing on the national circuit—particularly at larger tournaments such as Yale and Emory—have begun exclusively reading direct quotations when introducing evidence. These quotations are drawn from “cut cards.” If opponents request to see evidence, debaters must provide these cards (often via email) so their opponents may review them during their three minutes of preparation time. Advocates of reading direct quotations argue that this practice is superior to paraphrasing and have encouraged others to adopt it as a community standard. One method of doing so is through “paraphrase theory.” In this context, a debater will argue, in a round, that the judge should penalize a team that paraphrased—by awarding them a loss or entirely dropping arguments supported by paraphrased evidence—in order to establish a deterrent norm and incentivize the use of direct quotations.
Here is an example of a “cut card”:
Ian Bremmer, GZERO, 04/19/2021, “Putin's next move won't be a Baltic invasion that could unify NATO,” https://www.gzeromedia.com/the-red-pen/putins-next-move-wont-be-a-baltic-invasion-that-could-unify-nato // MH
An attack on the Balts may be fast or it may be victorious, but probably not both. And Putin knows this. Western leaders are conflicted about the alliance, but an assault on full-fledged NATO State and EU members is exactly the kind of provocation that could awaken it. Putin understands [and] this. He hardly wants to bring the alliance together as it's eroding. Low-cost efforts to steadily undermine legitimacy and grabbing targets of opportunity when available, that is much more Putin's speed.
When reading direct quotations, debaters typically present only the highlighted portions of the evidence (including bracketed clarifications as necessary).

entry.Resolution:
THR the complexity of language present in philosophical writing.
In ancient Greece, philosophers like Plato wrote dialogues meant to be read aloud and debated in public, and Aristotle aimed to classify ideas clearly, even when they were complex. Starting in the late 18th century, this changed. In Immanuel Kant’s Critique of Pure Reason (1781), Kant spends pages explaining ideas using phrases like “the transcendental unity of apperception,” which essentially means the mind’s ability to recognize its experiences as belonging to one self. In Martin Heidegger’s Being and Time, he invents new words such as Dasein to mean human existence and includes atypical language. Historically, the complexity arose as philosophy developed as a field.

British-style parliamentary democracies are systems in which the executive is drawn from and depends on the legislature, with governments requiring the confidence of a parliamentary majority to remain in office. Elections are typically party-centred, and the governing party or coalition controls the legislative agenda. In British style parliamentary democracies (Canada, the UK, Australia), strong party discipline refers to the requirement to vote along party lines in parliament, with failure resulting in sidelining/ostracization from the party (with rare exceptions for conscience votes where members may vote freely if the party decides its allowed). In contrast, weaker party discipline enables party members to vote freely without explicit consequences from their party.

For example, this could look like global movements primarily trying to help those in illiberal countries where women have few rights or domestic groups prioritizing helping women in the worst positions in their country (e.g. victims of domestic abuse) above other issues. A traditional approach refers to how feminist advocacy is done currently, with groups focusing on a variety of issues.

Lean In' promotes a cultural norm of assertiveness. It encourages women to assert themselves in the workplace through negotiating their salaries and working conditions, asking for raises and promotions, challenging gender biases, and being more confident in discussions (instead of being overly apologetic or taking a backseat role). 'Lean Out' focuses on deprioritizing traits like assertiveness, physical strength and dominance, and instead promotes the norms of deference, cooperation, considering the needs of others, and empathy.

THW replace the UN General Assembly’s one country, one vote system with a contribution-weighted voting system.
Under a “contribution-weighted voting” system, each country’s voting power would be proportional to its relative contributions to tackling global challenges. For example, if Country A contributes £5 billion, which is 5% of its GDP, and Country B contributes £10 billion, which is 1% of its GDP, then Country A would have greater voting power than Country B. Contributions can be monetary or non-monetary, for example providing soldiers for peacekeeping missions or agricultural donations.

THS private collegiate-level educational institutions adopting the Income-Share Schooling (ISS) model.
The Income-Share Schooling (ISS) model is one in which all admitted students do not pay any upfront tuition or fees. The private educational institution covers the cost of a students’ learning for all levels they offer and that the student chooses to take. After completing their education and earning above a minimum income threshold, they must pay a fixed percentage of their income for a set period of time under an income-share contract. The specific contractual terms (e.g. repayment rate, threshold, penalties) are set at the discretion of each institution.

entry.Resolution:
THP a notion of happiness guided by ataraxia rather than one guided by eudaimonia.
For Aristotle, happiness, called eudaimonia, is the ultimate goal of human life. It is achieved when the individual lives according to reason and practices virtues such as justice, courage, and temperance. To be happy, in this sense, is to fulfill one's moral and rational potential, contributing to the common good. For Pyrrho, happiness is achieved through ataraxia, a state of inner tranquility and emotional imperturbability. It arises when the individual suspends judgment about what is "good" or "bad," accepting the world as it is and not depending on acting morally or rationally, but on cultivating detachment.
entry.Name: NYPDL
entry.Topic Committee: Ethan Bordoff, Jane Kelly, Alex Doft, Maliha Thomas (equity)

entry.Resolution:
THBT AGI models should follow virtue ethics over deontology.
Artificial general intelligence (AGI) is a hypothetical stage in which an AI system can match or exceed the cognitive abilities of human beings across nearly all tasks. Deontology is a moral system that states there are certain rules which are absolute and should never be breached (e.g. murder, stealing, etc.). Virtue ethics is a moral system that states that to be moral, a person should have virtuous characteristics. These characteristics are a moderation of two vices. For example, between the extremes of cowardice and hubris, individuals should find the virtue of being brave.

entry.Resolution:
TH, as the animal rights movement, regret the dominance of anthropocentrism in discussions about animal rights.
Anthropocentrism is the doctrine that humans are the center of all things and are the most important entities in the universe. This doctrine is often used to evaluate or interpret the world based on human values and experiences. In discussions about animal rights, anthropocentrism is often manifested through human evaluations of animal rights based on human-like values (e.g., intelligence, sentience, etc.) and human moral scales. In contrast to anthropocentrism, other doctrines exist such as ecocentrism, which posits that humans are merely an equal part of the web of life. According to this view, ecocentrism criticizes the prioritization of certain species because of their similarities to humans and opposes the notion that "environmental protection is for the future of our children." Instead, it argues that every component of nature has its own intrinsic value and should be respected and protected in the present, not just for the long-term benefit of humanity.

entry.Resolution:
THBT countries in West and Central Africa should abandon the CFA Franc.
The CFA Franc is the name for two currencies used in 14 countries across West and Central Africa. The system dates back to 1945, when France created the “Franc of the French Colonies in Africa” to manage the economies of its colonies. After gaining independence in the 1960s, most of these countries chose to keep using the CFA Franc. The Franc has since been divided into two regional groups, one for West Africa and one for Central Africa, and each group has its own central bank. The CFA Franc operates through four main features. First, its value is pegged to the Euro at a rate of 1 Euro = 656 CFA Francs. Second, France guarantees that the CFA Franc can always be exchanged for Euros, which helps keep it stable. Third, every member country must keep half of its foreign currency reserves in a special account at the French Treasury. Fourth, French government representatives sit on the boards of both African central banks and have the power to veto important monetary decisions.
entry.Name: NYPDL
entry.Topic Committee: Ethan Bordoff, Zoe Manges, Alexander Georgatos

Two common approaches are “tech over truth” and “truth over tech.” For a judge utilizing a “tech over truth” approach, an argument is considered "true for the round" if the argument is (1) adequately warranted/justified and (2) insufficiently rebutted. For a judge utilizing a “truth over tech” approach, an argument is considered "true for the round" if the claim is (1) adequately warranted/justified, (2) insufficiently rebutted, and (3) plausibly true for the real world.

Afro-futurism reimagines the future via a black lens, voiding white supremacist thought and the structures that violently oppressed Black communities. Alternatively, Afro-pessimism is a lens of interpretation that accounts for, and focuses on the ongoing effects of racism, colonialism, and historical processes of enslavement including the trans-Atlantic slave trade and their impact on structural conditions as well as the personal, subjective, and lived experience and embodied reality of African Americans. The Parthenon Marbles, also known as the Elgin Marbles, are a collection of classical Greek sculptures and architectural pieces originally part of the Parthenon and other buildings on the Acropolis of Athens. Between 1801 and 1812, Lord Elgin, the British ambassador to the Ottoman Empire (which then ruled Greece), removed roughly half of the surviving sculptures and transported them to Britain. In 1816, the British Museum acquired these marbles, where they remain on public display today. The British Museum argues that the collection was legally obtained with permission from the Ottoman authorities, that it has been preserved and made accessible to a global audience, and that it forms part of a universal museum context representing world heritage.The Greek government, however, maintains that the marbles were taken under foreign occupation and therefore without legitimate consent. Greece has built the Acropolis Museum in Athens to house the sculptures in a controlled environment near their original site and has repeatedly requested their return.

entry.Resolution:
THR the U.S. government’s 2008 financial bailout of major banks.
In 2008, the United States entered a massive financial crisis—widely understood as primarily caused by major banks. Throughout the early 2000s, banks engaged in increasingly risky behavior: they issued subprime mortgages to borrowers who were unlikely to repay; bundled these risky loans into complex financial products like mortgage-backed securities (investments made up of many home loans packaged together and sold to investors, who in turn receive the homeowners’ monthly mortgage payments) and sold them across the global financial system while misrepresenting their safety. Banks also relied on extremely high levels of leverage, meaning they borrowed heavily to increase profits, which made them more vulnerable when asset prices fell. When homeowners began defaulting in large numbers, these mortgage-linked assets collapsed in value. Because banks were deeply invested in and interconnected through these products, the losses spread rapidly across the financial sector. This led to the failure of major institutions like Lehman Brothers, emergency rescues of Bear Stearns and AIG, and a global freezing of credit markets. At its peak, the U.S. was losing hundreds of thousands of jobs per month, unemployment climbed to 10%., millions of homeowners faced foreclosure, and stock markets plummeted, shrinking retirement accounts, pensions, and savings. To prevent the collapse of the financial system, the U.S. government enacted the Troubled Asset Relief Program (TARP) in 2008, authorizing $700 billion to stabilize major banks. The bailout injected capital into banks, purchased distressed assets, and provided emergency loans.

One of the most significant measures taken was the complete halt of Russian oil imports. Due to this, the price of Russian Oil significantly decreased. Seeing opportunity, India dramatically increased its own importation of Russian Oil. In 2021, 2% of India’s energy imports came from Russia (India's primary oil sources before were Middle Eastern countries, particularly Iraq, Saudi Arabia, and the UAE)—in 2024, 40% came from Russia (in turn, they decreased imports from other countries roughly uniformly, though more from non-middle eastern countries). In August 2025, the US increased its sanctions on India by 25% as a result of their continued buying of Russian oil.

There are two primary ways for abolitionists to interpret the Constitution at this time. entry.Resolution:
THW legalize champerty.
Champerty is a type of litigation financing where a third party (such as an investor, company, or fund) gives money to someone to help them run a lawsuit in exchange for a portion of whatever money is won. If the lawsuit fails, the funder loses the money they invested and gets nothing back. Champerty is most commonly used in class actions, where a large group of people who experienced similar harm sue a company or institution together. Many class action law firms do not charge clients upfront; instead, they take a percentage of the money won at the end. When champerty is allowed, the payment structure usually works like this: Lawyers take about 33% of the total money won. Litigation funders (the third-party investors) get paid out of that 33%. The plaintiffs—the people bringing the case—receive the remaining 66%.

entry.Resolution:
THW mandate the inclusion of ‘right to regulate’ clauses in all ISDS provisions.
Typically included in bilateral or multilateral investment treaties, investor-state dispute settlement (ISDS) provisions enable foreign investors to bypass local courts and resolve disputes with states through a binding decision from an independent tribunal. entry.Resolution:
For famous historical artworks where traditional restorations would be unremovable (permanently alter the painting), THP Kachkine’s method of restoration to traditional methods.
Traditional restoration involves experts using chemical, X-ray, and UV analysis, along with a detailed knowledge of art history and chemistry, to determine what in a painting needs restoration. An expert then manually adds adhesive to chipping paint and paints sections where the original paint has been chipped away. MIT researcher Alex Kachkine has developed a new method to restore paintings. He scans paintings and applies AI algorithms to create digitally restored versions, mapping thousands of regions needing repair and identifying precise colors. This data is printed onto masks that are varnished onto the painting to reproduce the painting’s original appearance. entry.Resolution:
THBT medical institutions should adopt the progressive qualification criteria as opposed to the classical qualification criteria when awarding treatment.
Classical qualification criteria refer to the pre-established medical metrics used to determine which patients should receive treatments that are resource- or cost-intensive. These criteria generally aim to prioritise patients with the highest likelihood of a good prognosis and meaningful extension of life. For example, in organ transplantation, candidates with active infections, cancer, advanced age, or severe comorbidities are typically excluded. Progressive qualification criteria refer to medical decision-making frameworks that focus on broader social and ethical considerations when allocating resource-intensive treatments. Under this approach, priority might be given to individuals who play a significant role in supporting or uplifting their communities, or to those with multiple dependents who would be severely affected by their loss.

Funding for teacher recruitment goes toward scholarships, hiring incentives, recruitment campaigns, certification programs, mentorship, and university partnerships to attract, train, and retain qualified teachers.

entry.Resolution:
THP a world where a countercyclical global insurance fund is the main source of credit of nations as opposed to the Bretton-Woods Institutions.
The Bretton Woods Institutions, mainly the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank, were established after World War II to promote global financial stability and development. Both institutions are funded by member countries: wealthier nations contribute more and hold greater voting power. The IMF provides short-term financial assistance and policy advice to countries facing debt crises, often with strict conditions requiring austerity or structural reforms. The World Bank focuses on long-term development loans and infrastructure projects, funded through member contributions and global capital markets. A countercyclical global insurance fund, by contrast, is a system where countries contribute to a shared pool during economic growth periods, and the fund provides financial support to nations in recession, stabilizing economies without the same political or policy conditions attached.

entry.Resolution:
THR the Norm of Bilingualism in Canadian Politics.
Canada was colonized first by the French in the 17th Century, and later more expansively by the British. The Canadian Province of Quebec, the territory most heavily colonized by the French, has long held a unique identity centered around the primacy of the French language and has historically suffered from both a relative lack of economic development and from discrimination against Francophones in the labor market. Approximately a quarter of all Canadians are Francophones and over 80% of these Francophones reside in the Province of Quebec. Since 1969, Canada has officially been bilingual at the federal level, and all federal laws and services are available in both French and English. Lingering tensions led Quebec to hold referendums on secession in 1980 and 1995, both of which had a small majority voting against secession. Today, Quebec and Francophones hold an outsize role in Canadian politics, with half of Prime Ministers hailing from Quebec since 1968 and all being bilingual. There is a strong norm - enforced by some parties as rule - that candidates for party leadership and by extension federal premiership be bilingual.

This house regrets the use of exotic animals as tools for diplomacy.
Panda diplomacy refers to China's practice of sending giant pandas to other countries, primarily as a tool of diplomacy and wildlife conservation. Initially, pandas were gifted, but since 1984, they have been leased due to a policy change. This strategy is a form of soft power, aiming to foster positive international relations and boost China's image abroad by leveraging the pandas' universal appeal. In 2024, Malaysia's Plantation and Commodities Minister Johari Abdul Ghani had suggested giving orangutans to major palm oil importers to bolster relations.

entry.Resolution:
This House Opposes the norm to prefer the natural to the artificial.
The “natural” is typically understood as something occurring in nature without human intervention (e.g., fruits, ecosystems, unmodified genes, untreated materials). The “artificial” is something created, modified, or enhanced by humans (e.g., synthetic drugs, GMOs, lab-grown foods, engineered environments, or digital creations). Many cultures and ethical frameworks valorize the “natural” over the “artificial,” associating it with purity, authenticity, and health. This motion asks whether that preference should be challenged.

entry.Resolution:
This House supports the "Bad Man" approach in policy making.
The term "bad man" in legal theory refers to a hypothetical individual who is solely concerned with the practical consequences of legal rules, particularly the potential for punishment, rather than with moral or ethical considerations. This "bad man" is interested in predicting how the law will be applied to their actions, focusing on the material consequences like fines or imprisonment, rather than on whether those actions are morally right or wrong.

entry.Resolution:
THO FIDE Women’s Titles.
The international chess body FIDE (Fédération Internationale des Échecs) awards titles for outstanding performance—Grandmaster (GM) is the highest, followed by International Master (IM), FIDE Master (FM), and Candidate Master (CM). These titles are available to all players. FIDE also awards women’s titles—Woman Grandmaster (WGM), Woman International Master (WIM), Woman FIDE Master (WFM), and Woman Candidate Master (WCM)—exclusively to female players, with requirements roughly 200 Elo points lower than the corresponding open titles. Only 10–11% of professional chess players globally are women, and of the ~1,722 Grandmasters, only ~37 are women. There are currently around 326 WGMs and 856 WIMs.

entry.Resolution:
THBT governments should prioritize supply-side solutions over demand-side and redistributive solutions to address housing crises in major cities.
In many major cities, housing costs have risen rapidly due to population growth, urbanization, and limited new development. Economists broadly agree that two leading strategies can reduce housing costs: Supply-side solutions aim to increase the total number of housing units, primarily through zoning reform, easing building restrictions, and incentivising private development. Demand-side and redistributive solutions aim to help individuals afford housing through government interventions such as rent control, public/social housing, rental subsidies, or taxes on vacant homes. While both approaches can coexist, governments often have limited resources and must prioritize one approach in both funding and political capital.
entry.Name: NYPDL
entry.Topic Committee: Ethan Bordoff, Zoe Manges, Alex Doft, Maliha Thomas (equity)

entry.Resolution:
In a liberal democracy, THP Norway’s trial system for major crimes to the US’.
In Norway, serious criminal cases often use “lay judges,” who sit with professional judges. Higher courts typically have three professionals and four lay judges. Lay judges are ordinary citizens appointed for four-year terms by (elected) municipal councils, and are supposed to reflect the country’s demographics. They deliberate and vote with professional judges on both guilt and sentencing. Decisions are made by majority vote. Most lay judges can expect to hear only a few cases during their four-year term. In the US, juries of 12 randomly selected citizens decide only on guilt or liability, deliberating separately from the judge until they reach a unanimous decision. Judges oversee procedure and determine sentencing (except in limited death penalty cases). In both countries, except for special circumstances, you cannot opt out of serving as a lay judge/juror, but those determined to have special interests in a trial that prevent their decisions from being unbiased cannot serve as a lay judge/juror for that trial.

entry.Resolution:
TH, as a popular and expanding new fast food chain, W adopt the franchise system over the corporate system.
A franchise is a type of license that grants a franchisee access to a franchisor's proprietary business knowledge, processes, reputation and trademarks, thus allowing the franchisee to sell a product or service under the franchisor's business name (e.g. most McDonalds’ and Taco bells are franchises). In exchange for acquiring a franchise, the franchisee usually pays the franchisor an initial start-up fee and annual licensing fees. On the other hand, a corporation is a distinct legal entity that is owned by its shareholders and managed by a board of directors. The board makes major business decisions, sets company policy, and oversees the corporation’s officers. Unlike a franchise, a corporation runs all of its business outlets (e.g. this is how Shake Shack and Chipotle operate).

entry.Resolution:
TH, as the founder of a new religion, W choose to use the Revelation Model over the Closed-Canon Model.
The Closed-Canon Model sees religious doctrine as fixed, based on a closed canon of scripture, and any developments are through interpretation rather than new revelations. For example, the Roman Catholic Church considers the Bible and teachings of the early Church Fathers as complete, and that public revelation ended with the death of the last apostle. The Revelation Model allows new beliefs to be introduced through revelations received by living prophets and apostles. Doctrine can evolve over time, and new scriptures can be added to the canon. For instance, the process by which the Mormon Church accepts new beliefs involves revelation to the modern day prophets and apostles, council decision as to whether to present the revelation, communication of the revelation to the Church, member acceptance through sustaining votes, and subsequent implementation.

entry.Resolution:
Assuming feasibility, THS the transfer of control of the US federal funds rate from the FOMC to a specially built AI model whose goal is to maintain a 2% inflation rate.
The Federal Reserve is the central banking system of the United States. The Fed considers itself “independent” because its decisions do not have to be approved by anyone and the terms of the members of the board of governors are 14 years long. It is governed by the presidentially appointed board of governors. Twelve regional banks regulate private banks. The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) sets the US federal funds rate, which influences market interest rates, in an attempt to stabilize inflation at its target of 2%. The FOMC consists of the board of governors and the regional bank presidents. The FOMC has been criticized for its inflation management, perceived lack of transparency, and role in economic downturns. Trump has recently pressured Fed Chair Jerome Powell to cut interest rates, criticized his leadership, and nominated allies to succeed him when he is “out of there.” Fed board members can only be removed “for cause,” traditionally interpreted as misconduct or incapacity, and Powell has maintained a commitment to independence.

entry.Resolution:
THBT the EU should stop the implementation of CBAM.
The EU currently has an EU-wide carbon cap with an emissions trading market. A Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) is a policy designed to encourage global adoption of carbon reduction practices and protect domestic industries from unfair competition due to differing environmental standards. It does so by adjusting the carbon cost of imported goods produced with high emissions, like steel or cement. Importers calculate the product’s embedded carbon and pay a fee (to the EU) equivalent to the EU carbon price. For example, if producing imported steel emitted 2 tons of CO₂ per ton of steel, and the EU carbon price is €50/ton, the importing country must pay the EU €100 per ton of steel as a CBAM fee. If the exporting country already taxed the good’s emissions, the CBAM fee is reduced to avoid double taxation. The EU is implementing CBAM, applying in its definitive regime from 2026, while the current transitional phase lasts between 2023 and 2025. Yet, BRICs countries and other developing countries have shown resistance to CBAM.

entry.Topic Committee: Ethan Bordoff, Jane Kelly, Andy Montvelisky, Maliha Thomas (equity)

entry.Resolution:
THW not reallocate seats.
Info slide: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), led by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, currently does not hold an absolute majority in the Lok Sabha, but retains a majority through the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) coalition with other parties. The BJP has been criticized for their Hindu nationalist, far-right ideology, as well as spreading disinformation about and demonizing Muslims. Under the BJP, India has experienced significant democratic backsliding. Modi and the BJP have traditionally faced resistance from the wealthy, highly-educated southern states (e.g. Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Telangana), whereas they are more popular in the North. The southern states currently only account for 20% of India’s total population. The Lok Sabha is the lower house of India’s Parliament, with seats allocated to each state based on their population size in 1971. However, the number of seats per state has been frozen since then to avoid punishing states like Kerala and Tamil Nadu for highly effective family planning programs that have resulted in lower population sizes. The Lok Sabha seat freeze is set to expire in 2026.

entry.Resolution:
THP rule-based utilitarianism to act-based utilitarianism.
INFO SLIDE: Act utilitarianism says that when faced with a choice, you should ask what choice in that specific situation looks like  it will maximize the greater good, then do that. Rule utilitarianism says you should ask what rules, if followed consistently, would maximize the greater good, then follow those rules consistently even in cases where the outcome is sub-optimal. John Stuart Mill was the most famous proponent of rule utilitarianism. He cited censorship as one example where we should commit to a rule of not censoring people, arguing that following the rule consistently will get better results than allowing ourselves to censor people on a case-by-case basis.

entry.Resolution:
THBT the Mexican feminist movement should advocate for the creation of anti-monuments, as opposed to the creation of 'positive monuments'.
INFO SLIDE: In Mexico, anti-monuments are installed during protests to recall a tragic event or unfulfilled demand for justice. They usually critique national symbols and monuments with socio-political messaging. Examples include La Glorieta de las Mujeres que Luchan (Roundabout of the Women Who Fight), which was installed as a reminder of Mexico's gendered violence as well as the ongoing fight for equal rights, and 49 ABC, which commemorates the 49 children who died in the 2009 Hermosillo daycare center fire. The center was funded by the Mexican federal government. There are also movements to install 'positive monuments' to celebrate the legacy of minorities as a part of Mexico's national identity. Examples include a proposal to replace the Christopher Columbus statue with a replica of La joven de Amajac (The Young Women of Amajac), a pre-Hispanic sculpture depicting an indigenous woman and El Yanga, an enslaved African man who led a revolution and established a community of freed people.

entry.Resolution:
THP trade conflicts between member states be resolved through regional organizations as opposed to internal arbitration within the WTO.
Article 25 of the WTO's (World Trade Organization) Dispute Settlement Understanding allows for arbitration as an alternative dispute resolution mechanism, provided both parties agree to it. This process is flexible, enabling the parties to define the scope, select arbitrators, and establish procedures. The arbitration award is binding and must be consistent with WTO agreements, with outcomes notified to the Dispute Settlement Body.

entry.Resolution:
THBT the US and Canada should ban Mandatory Binding Arbitration.
Mandatory Binding Arbitration is a contractual provision in which both parties to a contract waive their right to sue one another in court for damages related to a perceived breach of contract. Instead, in the instance of a perceived contractual violation, members must undergo arbitration, an alternative form of dispute resolution in which a mutually agreed upon private arbiter determines both the legitimacy of the alleged violation as well as the potential punishment. MBA clauses can also often include other stipulations such as waiving one's right to appeal the decision or to join class action lawsuits.

Historically, the finances of the Vatican has always been shrouded in mystery as it publishes little to no information about it. The Institute for the Works of Religion or the more widely known Vatican Bank, has been subject to numerous frauds and scandals in the past few decades.

entry.Resolution:
THBT religions should take a progressive revelation approach, rather than a traditional revelation approach.
Progressive revelation refers to the belief that divine truths gradually change with humanity over time, through prophets or other chosen individuals. This understanding implies that God's communication with humanity is ongoing and adaptable to the changing needs of society. For example, the prohibition on pork consumption was due to this animal being a transmitter of diseases in the past, but in the present-day, it would be morally permissible following the discovery of antibiotics. On the other hand, traditional revelation believes that God's message is eternal and does not change over time. According to this perspective, divine truths are fixed and do not change with human circumstances or social advancements. It is believed that God has transmitted complete and definitive truths through sacred scriptures or other specific revelations, and that these messages should be interpreted and followed without significant changes throughout history.
entry.Name: NYPDL
entry.Topic Committee: Adrian Turkedjiev, Rodda John, Amber Safir, Eloise Biddle-Gottesman

entry.Resolution:
TH, as Sir Gawain, W kill the dragon.
It is the age after King Arthur’s reign. There is a magical dragon up in the mountains whose breath has created a magical mist over Arthur’s kingdom. As a result of the mist, people have an extremely weak grip on their long-term memories: when separated for long periods of time, parents forget their children; lovers forgets lovers; village councils adjudicate on a problem and then have no recollection of it ever happening. A generation ago, Arthur and his knights waged a successful war to protect Britons against the Saxons and carved out a great kingdom. In order to stop future generations of Saxons from continuing the cycle of violence, the Knights slaughtered entire villages. Arthur, recognizing that this would not end the cycle of violence but rather worsen it, asked Merlin to enchant the dragon such that the memories of this genocide were lost. Today, the Britons are safe in Arthur’s kingdom and live in harmony alongside a minority of Saxons. Neighboring Saxon kingdoms look at the Saxon minorities as the best way to wage war against Arthur’s kingdom and expand. Sir Gawain, knight and nephew of Arthur, the last surviving member of the old King's faithful, walks the crypts over the skulls of Saxon babies and questions if they were in the right. Gawain is now an elderly yet formidable as ever warrior who could dispose of the dragon swiftly. Yet, so far, he has chosen not to, fearing the violence that would descend upon the land if the Saxons regained their memories of the violence.
entry.Name: NYPDL
entry.Topic Committee: Adrian Turkedjiev, Rodda John, Amber Safir, Eloise Biddle-Gottesman

Over centuries, society adapted to this and has developed an entire culture around the dragon, including religious beliefs that justify the sacrifices and government bureaucracy (Department of Offerings to the Great Entity, or DOGE) that facilitates them and compensates those left behind. The sacrifices are frequent and large enough that almost everyone in the community has lost a loved one during their lifetime. Science has now advanced to the point where a material has been developed that can pierce the dragon's scales, making it possible to launch an attack on the dragon. However, the attack may fail, and the dragon may retaliate against the whole community.

entry.Resolution:
THW disallow patent rights for any technology that was developed using HeLa cells.
Henrietta Lacks died in 1951, aged 31, of an aggressive cervical cancer. Months earlier, doctors at the Johns Hopkins Hospital in Baltimore, Maryland, had taken samples of her cancerous cells while diagnosing and treating the disease. They gave some of that tissue to a researcher without Lacks’s knowledge or consent. In the laboratory, her cells turned out to have an extraordinary capacity to survive and reproduce; they were, in essence, immortal. The researcher shared them widely with other scientists, and they became a workhorse of biological research. Today, work done with HeLa cells underpins much of modern medicine; they have been involved in key discoveries in many fields, including cancer, immunology and infectious disease. One of their most recent applications has been in research for vaccines against COVID-19. Lacks was a Black woman. The hospital where her cells were collected was one of only a few that provided medical care to Black people. None of the biotechnology or other companies that profited from her cells passed any money back to her family. For decades after her death, doctors and scientists repeatedly failed to ask her family for consent as they revealed Lacks’s name publicly, gave her medical records to the media, and even published her cells’ genome online.
entry.Name: NYPDL
