Former Racing 92 Neurologist Dr Chermann has come forward without consulting Sexton to say “I think Johnny Sexton has had around 30 concussions across his entire career. It’s true that it’s enormous.” “If Sexton plays on Sunday, it’s sad for him. This is what really inspires me: sadness.” Dr Barry O’Driscoll is the former medical adviser to World Rugby who stepped down in 2012 to protest against the governing body’s concussion protocols - namely the head injury assessment (HIA) and current six-day return to play protocols. After Dr Chermann's statement, he came forward to again state that there is no scientific basis to the world rugby rules of allowing a player to play 6 days post head injury.

entry.Resolution:
Capitalism is failing into techno-feudalism.
INFOSLIDE: Techno-feudalism is a concept that describes the shift from a capitalist economy to a system where a few dominant technology corporations and digital platforms exert feudal-like control over markets, labor, and data. In this model, wealth and power are concentrated in the hands of tech giants that act as digital landlords, extracting rents from users, workers, and smaller businesses through platform fees, data monetization, and algorithmic control. Unlike traditional capitalism, where competition and production drive profits, techno-feudalism relies on monopolistic dominance, network effects, and surveillance capitalism to maintain control.

INFOSLIDE: Effective Accelerationism (often abbreviated as e/acc) is an emerging ideological movement that advocates for the rapid advancement of technology, industry, and economic growth as a means to drive human progress. It contrasts with decelerationist views, which emphasize caution, regulation, or limitations on technological development due to concerns about risks such as environmental damage or artificial intelligence threats.

The citizen welfare standard is preferable to the consumer welfare standard in legal doctrine.
INFOSLIDE: The consumer welfare standard holds that businesses should only be stopped from merging or acting in anti-competitive ways that hurt consumers, like raising prices or lowering quality. The citizen welfare standard looks at broader impacts, considering negative externalities such as privacy, the environment, and democracy.

entry.Resolution:

He is threatening China, Mexico and Canada with higher rates within days and has contemplated higher levies globally, with countries having a high trade surplus (i.e., countries exporting more than they import) being singled out. Japan could be hit hard. It has significant manufacturing capacity in Mexico, Canada and China and maintains a persistent and sizable trade surplus with the United States, while the yen has been weakening since 2020. During the last Trump administration, Japan often worked to fill the power vacuum the US left. When President Trump pulled the United States out of the Trans-Pacific Partnership in 2017, for instance, Japan played a significant role in preserving it as the Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership with the remaining members.

The law, signed by Joe Biden, required ByteDance (TikTok's China-based parent company) to sell the app or face a ban effective January 19, 2025. Lawmakers argue that ByteDance’s ties to the Chinese government make TikTok vulnerable to foreign influence, posing a national security risk. If upheld, the ban would remove TikTok from app stores, prevent updates, and eventually degrade app functionality. Existing users may retain access temporarily, but workarounds like VPNs could bypass restrictions. ByteDance can avoid the ban by selling TikTok to a non-Chinese owner.

entry.Resolution:
THS courts piercing the corporate veil when plaintiffs allege a company has violated environmental regulations.
Most companies operate under limited liability, meaning owners' personal assets will be protected if the company faces legal or financial challenges. This is sometimes referred to as a “corporate veil.” “Piercing the corporate veil” is a legal practice where a court will hold a company's shareholders, directors, and/or officers liable for that company's debts or wrongful actions. Right now, many jurisdictions do not pierce the corporate veil except in cases where corporate actors have engaged in fraudulent behavior. Although a plaintiff usually sues and wins against a company before requesting veil-piercing, plaintiffs may also request veil-piercing without suing a whole company.

Consequently, he comes up with this proposal for elite universities: “Of the 40,000-plus applicants, winnow out those who are unlikely to flourish at Harvard or Stanford, those who are not qualified to perform well and to contribute to the education of their fellow students. This would leave the admissions committee with, say, 30,000 qualified contenders, or 25,000, or 20,000. Rather than engage in the exceedingly difficult and uncertain task of trying to predict who among them are the most surpassingly meritorious, choose the entering class by lottery. In other words, toss the folders of the qualified applicants down the stairs, pick up 2,000 of them, and leave it at that.”

entry.Resolution:
THBT Brazil should declare military support for the territorial integrity of the Guyana.
In 2015, Guyana discovered large quantities of oil in the oceanic perimeter of the Essequibo region. This region occupies around 70% of Guyana's territory and is home to around 20% of the country's population, but is historically the subject of dispute with Venezuela, which has claimed the region since the end of the 18th century, claiming that the natural border between the countries is the east bank of the Essequibo River. In 1899, the US mediated an arbitration court that ceded the Essequibo region to the United Kingdom to the detriment of Venezuela, but this judgment was annulled due to procedural problems. In 1966, when Guyana became independent, the countries tried the Geneva Agreement to end the conflict, but were unable to reach a consensus. In 2018, Guyana filed a request for the International Court of Justice (ICJ) to ratify the current borders, but there has been no judgment yet. In October 2023, the Venezuelan government publicly declared its intention to annex the Essequibo region and scheduled a popular referendum to consult the Venezuelan population and decide on the annexation of the territory. The referendum is likely to have a result in favor of annexation and Venezuelan troops have already been deployed to the border.
entry.Tags: International Relations, Military, Non-US, the Americas

The President of Brazil’s government, Jair Bolsonaro, has been harshly criticized for encouraging more deforestation to stimulate Brazil's own economic development. However, these EU nations said they will block the agreement with Brazil and other countries unless Bolsonaro agrees to do more to tackle Amazonian destruction.

entry.Resolution:
THW walk away.
There is a city called Omelas where all the citizens live perfectly fulfilled and happy lives. Buildings are beautiful, crops are plentiful, there is no disease, no crime, and no sorrow of any kind. On the day they reach adulthood, every citizen is taken into the citadel, to a room in the basement. There, in the deepest dungeon, they find a child, malnourished and sick, chained against the wall, in the utmost misery a human being can endure. They know that if the child were comforted, if it were allowed to enjoy a solitary moment of happiness, that the beauty of the city above would crumble, and disease, crime and want would become a part of the peoples lives. For that reason, the child will never be allowed to leave by the city. Every citizen in Omelas knows it is there, and they have all agreed to live with it. Occasionally, a citizen, man or woman, young or old, will walk through the gate on the edge of the city. They will venture into the desert that surrounds the city for as far as can be seen, walk over the horizon, and never be seen or heard from again. They are known only as The Ones who Walk Away from Omelas. It is not possible to save the child.

entry.Resolution:
THP atomic communitarianism to contemporary liberal democracy.
“Atomic communitarianism” refers to a system of government in which the state is divided into semi autonomous zones, organized on the basis of political philosophy. For example, an atomic communitarian civilization might be composed of a libertarian community with a fully deregulated economy and low taxes, a community that is functionally a Scandinavian-style social democracy, an anarcho-primitivist community where people live in a state of unchained nature with no laws, and more. Each community contributes financially to a central government and military force, whose only duties are to prevent communities from causing harm to each other, ensuring freedom to move from one community to another, and preventing unwanted ideological contamination (e.g., keeping televisions and cell phones out of the anarcho-primitivist community, or keeping explicit media out of the fundamentalist Christian community). The central government would allow each community to submit an information package on its values, which would be distributed to every 18-year old.

INFO SLIDE: "School choice" programs are those which give parents more options regarding where their children go to school. The most prominent school choice program is school vouchers. In this system, each family can still enroll their child in public school as normal, but if they want to send their child to private school, the government will help them pay tuition by taking whatever money they would have spent educating the child at public school, removing that money from the public school's budget, and instead applying it to the cost of tuition at the private school of the parents' choosing. This can be summarized as "the tax dollars travel with the child."

entry.Resolution:
The "pink tide" in Latin America has done more harm than good.
INFO SLIDE: The "pink tide" is a turn towards leftist political movements in Latin American nations in the late 20th and 21st centuries. The dissolution of the Soviet Union allowed leftist parties to operate independent of fears of Soviet control, and reduced the intensity of anti-communist intervention from the United States. Many leftist parties took this opportunity to consolidate power. Economic difficulties across Latin America intensified this process in the 21st century. Many argue that the death of Hugo Chavez marked the end to this trend, and by the mid-2010s, Latin American governments began to move rightward.

entry.Resolution:
THS integration of mainstream and para-athlete event schedules, governing bodies and decision-making.
The status quo is there are two governing bodies: the International Olympic Committee (IOC) and the International Paralympic Committee (IPC). While the organizations have a partnership agreement which sets out matters of cooperation and financial support, they make decisions separately (e.g. the decision to ban all Russian athletes from the 2016 Paralympics due to doping, vs. allowing some Russian athletes to compete in the 2016 Olympics). Additionally, the Olympic Games and the Paralympic Games are held separately, although the partnership agreement requires the same host for both. The IPC also undertakes its own advocacy for broader para athlete issues.

entry.Resolution:
THR Elon Musk’s purchasing of Twitter.
Elon Musk initiated an acquisition of American social media company Twitter, Inc. on April 14, 2022, and concluded it on October 28, 2022. Musk had begun buying shares of the company in January 2022, becoming its largest shareholder by April with a 9.1 percent ownership stake. entry.Resolution:
This House believes that the US should become a unitary state.
Info Slide: In unitary states, such as France, the national government has final say on all matters of government. By contrast, the US is currently a federation, as outlined in its Constitution (see Amendment 10 and Article I Section 8). This means the federal government has final say over some matters (e.g. foreign policy), while the 50 state governments have final say over other matters (e.g. most of education policy). This balance of power between the federal and state governments has shifted throughout US history.

entry.Resolution:
If the technology existed, this House, as a parent, would use the Child Chip.
Info slide: The Child Chip is painlessly and safely implanted into babies' brains after birth. The technology allows a parent to see the child’s location at all times and use their smartphone to see what the child is currently seeing and implement content restrictions on what the child can see (e.g., the audio would be dampened and the child would see disturbing content in real life as merely a blur). When the child’s stress levels go up, the parent will receive a notification and can alter any settings remotely. The chip will be permanently and irreversibly disabled once the child reaches 16.

entry.Resolution:
THW replace Sales Tax with Value-Added Tax (VAT) in the United States.
Info: A Value-Added Tax assesses the value of a given product at every stage of development and taxes it based on that value. As the product goes down the production line any added value gets taxed. A VAT is different from a sales tax in that a sales tax is only levied once, at the end of production after the consumer purchases the product. Contrarily the VAT is paid at every stage of production. However, every business along the value chain receives a tax credit for the VAT already paid. The end consumer does not, making it a tax on final consumption.

Odious debt is a legal concept that occurs when a country’s government switches and the new government does not want to pay for the debts acquired by previous governments. Odious debt is acquired only through countries when the government changes through internal or external revolution.

entry.Resolution:
THBT the Supreme Court should overturn Chevron Deference.
Under Chevron deference, courts are obligated to defer to experts within the administrative state to make decisions on the interpretations of vague congressional rulings. For example, if Congress passed a law saying the Department of the Interior could create wind farms as long as the environmental impact was less harmful than the possible benefits, the experts within the Department of the Interior would be in charge of conducting the research to find out if the environmental impact was less harmful than the possible benefits. The Courts would then have to defer to whatever the Department of the Interior decided was the smartest environmental/social decision.

entry.Resolution:
In the Game of Life, players begin the game by choosing the college path or the career path. To enter the college path, you must pay a large amount of your allotted funds and play ~ 3 turns without getting a job or making money. By the time you graduate college, though, you get to choose a job making around 80 thousand dollars. The career path, on the other hand, allows you to get a job instantly, but tends to pay a lot less, averaging 30 thousand dollars. Typically, when you choose the career path, it is hard to have the funds to buy a house and pay for things later on in the game.
THR the narrative that a college degree is the path to success in life.

entry.Resolution:
THS removing Donald Trump from the Republican primary ballot.
On December 19, 2023, the Colorado Supreme Court voted to remove Trump from the Colorado Republican Primary ballot, citing that the 14th amendment’s ban on insurrectionists taking office covers his conduct on January 6th, 2021. Since then, Maine has also removed Trump, and states such as Illinois, Oregon, Massachusetts, and more are petitioning removal. However, states like Michigan and Minnesota have ruled that they cannot interfere with the Republican Party’s nominations. Every single GOP primary candidate has opposed the decision to remove Trump from the ballot with businessman Vivek Ramaswamy volunteering to remove himself from the ballot in states where Trump has been removed and urging the other primary candidates to do the same.

entry.Resolution:
You are a doctor in the future.  A patient comes into your office looking incredibly ill, and you quickly identify their ailment—a failing heart.  They could potentially die without treatment.  In fact, they pass out in your office.  Luckily, you know all that is required is a simple surgery in which you can give your patient a synthetic heart and they will be as good as new.  Yet, as you are preparing to take the patient into surgery, a small medical card falls out of their pocket indicating that for religious reasons, they do not want any synthetic organs.  If you do not install the synthetic heart, the patient will die.  But, if you do, you will be violating the patient's wishes.
THW install the synthetic heart.

All that said, every person and thing you encounter within the machine is simply a programmed simulation and nothing and no one you encounter will be real.  Entering the simulation is a life long decision—if you choose to live in the simulation, you can never go back to the real world.
THW enter the machine.

Legend has it that on every Halloween night, the ghosts of the Allington family return to reclaim their ancestral home, regardless of the current inhabitants. This year, the town's mayor, residing in the mansion, finds himself embroiled in a debate with the town's eccentric historians, who argue that the ethereal inhabitants possess an undeniable right to reclaim their lost property.
THBT the ghosts of Allington Mansion have a moral right to that property.

entry.Resolution:
THP the equal-weight view over the steadfast view of peer-disagreement.
Background: Peer disagreement is when people of similar levels of intelligence and knowledge about a given subject disagree about what is true. For example, if two biologists disagree about how much a duck weighs. How do you resolve this difference? The equal weight view says that one ought to change their view based on what a peer says to meet in the middle. The steadfast view says that one ought to have courage in their conviction and stand behind their view even under disagreement.

entry.Resolution:
THR increasing the amount of deposits that are insured by the government at Signature and Silicon Valley Bank.
The Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) is an independent agency created by Congress to maintain stability and public confidence in the US financial system.  One of the main things the FDIC does to support its mission is that it insures deposits at member banks up to $250,000 per depositor, per insured bank in the event the bank goes bankrupt or is placed in receivership.  Funding for such insurance comes from charges on member banks, not from general tax revenues. Last month, Silicon Valley Bank and Signature Bank were both placed into receivership after depositors began withdrawing money rapidly.  As an example, deposits at Silicon Valley Bank declined from $173B at the end of 2022, to under $60B in March when the FDIC stepped in.  After taking over both banks, the FDIC announced that all deposits at those banks (only those two banks) would be insured, regardless of the amount.

entry.Resolution:
A music label, also known as a record label, is a brand of music recordings and music videos that is owned by a company. The company generally has marketing teams and press teams to promote its artists in addition to publishing their music. Music labels are categorized into major labels and indie labels, with major labels representing 60% to 70% of the music industry. The typical advantages of signing a music label deal include more publicity for an artist and increased access to resources for music production. At the same time, label deals often stipulate a high level of royalties collected by the label company and partial loss of creative control.
THP a world in which music labels do not exist.

entry.Resolution:
Puritanism was an extreme form of Christianity that emerged in 16th Century England. Dissenting from the Church of England, many Puritans fled to North America - establishing the Massachusetts Bay Colony. Until the very end of the 17th Century, Puritans were the Hegemonic force in the Colony. Church and State were intimately linked in these times - the Puritans believing themselves to be in a covenant with God, seeking to strictly enforce correct moral and religious behavior in order to secure God’s blessing. Puritans believed in the active existence of the Devil and Demons, as well as Witches - persons with supernatural powers gained through collaboration with the Demonic. Seemingly unexplainable phenomena - eg., crop failures, illness, unusually harsh weather - were commonly blamed on the work of Witches.
Instead of staging Witch Trials, This House, as the leadership of a Puritan colonial town in the 1600s Massachusetts, would abstain from the persecution of Witches.

entry.Resolution:
American Girl Dolls are a series of very popular dolls, where each unique character created into a doll has an accompanying book that outlines their story. entry.Resolution:
The temple of Artemis was widely considered the most beautiful building in the ancient western world, until a man named Herostratus burned it down. Asked why, he said that he wanted his name to be remembered forever, regardless of the cause. The ancient Greeks conspired to prevent this by erasing all mention of his name so he would be forgotten instead. (They also killed him.) But the ancient historian Theopompus recorded the name and so Herostratus is remembered.
As Theopompus, THW not record the name of Herostratus.

entry.Resolution:
“Perhaps no one has yet been truthful enough about what 'truthfulness' is.” 
THP a coherence model of truth to a correspondence model of truth.
The correspondence model of truth holds that a proposition is true if it corresponds to the way the world is.  A valid argument would be: apples are red because I see that they are red, thus ‘apples are red’ is true. The coherence model of truth that a proposition is true if it coheres to existing sets of truths.  The coherence may be internal to a personal set of beliefs that are accessible to a subject. When choosing between two new scientific theories, for example, a coherence thinker is more likely to choose the theory that coheres with existing scientific theories as opposed to choosing the theory that destroys existing thought.

You also learn that he does not immediately kill his victims, but put them in positions where they face a choice that is made difficult for them because of their own particular character flaws, and survive if and only if they do the right thing. Everyone who has survived the Jigsaw Killer’s tests has turned over a new leaf and abandoned their old ways. You finally catch the Jigsaw Killer, who is terminally ill. He professes a belief that every bad person must have a chance to reform. He tells you he still has people to test, and asks you to let him go. For the purposes of the motion, his tests are perfectly effective, and nobody will find out if you let him go.
THW let him go.

THBT there should be a mandatory cap and trade program for carbon emissions in the United States.
Cap and trade is a system designed to limit pollution in the atmosphere. The cap places a firm limit on how much large companies are allowed to emit, which is lowered over time. The trade is a market that enables companies to purchase and sell allowances that let them emit only a certain amount, as supply and demand set the price.

You are a train director driving a train down a railway. As you approach the station, you realize that the brakes on your train do not work. Ahead of you, you see a group of three construction workers on the tracks. There is no time for the construction workers to leave the tracks, and since the brakes are not working, there is nothing you can do to prevent the train from hitting - and killing - the three construction workers. However, you notice there is an alternative path on the railway that leads to a different track, where there is only one construction worker sitting on the tracks. There is a switch in your train that, if flipped, would turn your train onto the “alternative” path. If you flipped the switch, you would save the lives of the three construction workers on the main path, but in so doing, would kill the singular construction worker on the “alternative” path.
THW flip the switch.

entry.Resolution:
Info Slide: In 2017, Teamsters Local 174 went on strike against concrete supplier Glacier Northwest. Consequently, mixed concrete hardened and spoiled. Glacier Northwest sued the union, alleging that the union timed the strike to create intentional property damage. Teamsters Local 174 argued that the strike was federally protected by the National Labor Relations Act, preventing the company from retaliating against the union for striking. The Washington Supreme Court ruled that the company’s claims were preempted under the Supreme Court’s 1959 decision in San Diego Building Trades Council v. Garmon, which blocks the state and municipal regulation of activities protected by federal labor law. The Supreme Court has agreed to review the case and consider whether an employer making common-law allegations of intentional destruction of property during a labor dispute constitutes an exception to federal labor law preemption of state lawsuits.
Resolved: In the case of Glacier Northwest, Inc. v. International Brotherhood of Teamsters Local Union No. 174, the Supreme Court of the United States should rule in favor of Glacier Northwest, Inc.

entry.Resolution:
Info Slide: Mutually preferred judging is a judge assignment system where debate teams rank judges on a preference scale prior to the tournament. When pairing rounds, rather than randomly assigning judges, Tabroom will evaluate the individually submitted rankings of both teams and attempt to assign the highest-ranked mutually preferred judge to each round. This is done by balancing preference (teams getting judges they rated highly) vs. mutuality (teams getting a judge that they and their opponents rated similarly) alongside tournament constraints.
Resolved: At high school parliamentary debate tournaments, random assignment of judges is preferable to mutually preferred judging.

INFO SLIDE: A technical high school education focuses highly on applicable skills, such as coding, cooking, engineering, public speaking and others. entry.Resolution:
You are a middle-aged person whose family runs the Bluth Company – a corrupt corporation.  You spend most of your time – work life and personal – with your family, but you consider yourself the only “honorable” member. You are at a company party on a boat, and you know that you are about to be named the new CEO of the Bluth Company.  Suddenly, you see boats with sirens; it’s the Securities and Exchange Commission (yes, the SEC has boats).  The SEC has come to arrest your father, who is the current CEO of the Bluth Company, for fraud, and will investigate other members of the family as well. You have crucial information that will likely exonerate yourself, but may also implicate other members of your family.
THW not cooperate with the SEC.
entry.Name: NYPDL

entry.Resolution:
You are an over-qualified chemistry teacher living in New Mexico.  You have a wife, a teenage son, and a daughter on the way.  Your brother-in-law is an agent with the Drug Enforcement Agency, and he has just been shot. Your wife offered to pay for his medical care (since he could not afford it), so now your family is hundreds of thousands of dollars in debt.  You know that you have the ability to create and make huge profits from methamphetamine.
THW produce and sell meth.
entry.Name: NYPDL

entry.Resolution:
You live in a world where people are divided into four nations based upon their ability to manipulate one of four corresponding elements: water, earth, fire, and air. In this world, there is one figure, the Avatar, who uniquely possesses the ability to manipulate all four elements and is charged with keeping peace between the peoples of each of the four elements. The figure reincarnates upon death. On your twelfth birthday, you are told three things by the elders of your community. One, you were born as the new Avatar, and your identity has been kept a secret from the rest of the world. Two, you will undergo intense training for the rest of your childhood to master the four elements. And finally, that they see omens of an impending war among the four nations.
THW publicize their identity as the Avatar.

entry.Resolution:
“Cloture” – a vote to end discussion and move to a vote – currently requires 60 votes in the Senate, and is used by minority parties to filibuster (i.e. block legislation) as they only need 41 votes to block a vote on legislation or an appointment. The filibuster has been removed for Judicial and Executive Branch appointments. As a Senate rule, the number of votes needed for cloture can be changed by a simple majority vote.
TH, as a Democratically controlled Senate, would set cloture at a simple majority and end the filibuster.

entry.Resolution:
You live in a town with an annual lottery. The lottery tradition is ancient and no one knows its origin or purpose, but it continues to be held every year. There is a popular belief that generations ago, the lottery saved the town from widespread hunger and crime, and that ever since, the town has enjoyed abundant harvests, safe streets, and overall prosperity. So what is the lottery? The lottery randomly selects one person to be stoned to death by all the people in the town, including the children, and life resumes normally afterwards for everyone — including the family of the murdered person.
Assuming you have the ability, THW stop the lottery.
entry.Name: NYPDL

entry.Resolution:
THW implement a ranked-choice voting system in US primary elections.
“A ranked-choice voting system is an electoral system in which voters rank candidates by preference on their ballots. If a candidate wins a majority of first-preference votes, he or she is declared the winner. If no candidate wins a majority of first-preference votes, the candidate with the fewest first-preference votes is eliminated. First-preference votes cast for the failed candidate are eliminated, lifting the second-preference choices indicated on those ballots. A new tally is conducted to determine whether any candidate has won a majority of the adjusted votes. The process is repeated until a candidate wins an outright majority.”

entry.Resolution:
There is a city called Omelas where all the citizens live perfectly fulfilled and happy lives. Buildings are beautiful, crops are plentiful, there is no disease, no crime, and no sorrow of any kind. On the day they reach adulthood, every citizen is taken into the citadel, to a room in the basement. There, in the deepest dungeon, they find a child, malnourished and sick, chained against the wall, in the utmost misery a human being can endure. They know that if the child were comforted, if it were allowed to enjoy a solitary moment of happiness, that the beauty of the city above would crumble, and disease, crime and want would become a part of the peoples lives. For that reason, the child will never be allowed to leave by the city. Every citizen in Omelas knows it is there, and they have all agreed to live with it. Occasionally, a citizen, man or woman, young or old, will walk through the gate on the edge of the city. They will venture into the desert that surrounds the city for as far as can be seen, walk over the horizon, and never be seen or heard from again.  They are known only as The Ones who Walk Away from Omelas.
Motion: THW walk away.
entry.Name: NYPDL

entry.Resolution:
There is a city called Omelas where all the citizens live perfectly fulfilled and happy lives. Buildings are beautiful, crops are plentiful, there is no disease, no crime, and no sorrow of any kind. On the day they reach adulthood, every citizen is taken into the citadel, to a room in the basement. There, in the deepest dungeon, they find a child, malnourished and sick, chained against the wall, in the utmost misery a human being can endure. They know that if the child were comforted, if it were allowed to enjoy a solitary moment of happiness, that the beauty of the city above would crumble, and disease, crime and want would become a part of the peoples lives. For that reason, the child will never be allowed to leave by the city. Every citizen in Omelas knows it is there, and they have all agreed to live with it. Occasionally, a citizen, man or woman, young or old, will walk through the gate on the edge of the city. They will venture into the desert that surrounds the city for as far as can be seen, walk over the horizon, and never be seen or heard from again.They are known only as The Ones who Walk Away from Omelas.
Motion: THW walk away.
entry.Name: NYPDL

Information slide: Music streaming is a service in which users can listen to a library of music without buying individual songs or albums. Each time a user listens to a song via the service, streaming companies pay royalties to record labels or independent artists with rights to that song. Royalties per listen are around $0.00735 (Apple Music), $0.00437 (Spotify), or $0.00133 (Pandora Premium). Users pay streaming companies a subscription fee or, in some cases, use a free version with advertisements and limited features.
Motion: This house regrets the rise of music streaming services.

entry.Resolution:
Information slide: In recent years, Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro has weakened democratic institutions in the country (e.g. he has censored media, imprisoned some political opponents, and filled courts with his supporters). Meanwhile, Venezuela has faced increasing economic difficulty and violence, with many struggling to access basic resources such as food and medicine. On January 10, 2019, Juan Guaidó, the President of the National Assembly (a legislative body) and member of the opposition, challenged Maduro’s claim to the Presidency. 54 countries, including the U.S. and most of South America, recognize Guaidó as Venezuela’s legitimate President, but Maduro continues to exercise power.
Motion: This house believes that the international community should intervene in Venezuela.

entry.Resolution:
Information Slide: The National Institutes of Health (NIH) is a federal government agency that invests $39.2 billion annually in medical research for the American people. The NIH is funded using taxpayer dollars, and its budget is set by Congress. Most of the $39.2 billion is awarded via competitive grants to research academics applying for research funding. Research priorities and funding allocation are determined by decision-makers who evaluate current opportunities and public health needs. In some cases, this leads to funding rates that do not correlate with US burdens of disease. For example, HIV/AIDS receives the 2nd largest amount of funding but is 45th of 75 in US disease burden. By contrast, coronary heart disease is 5th in US disease burden but receives the 18th largest amount of funding.
Motion: This house believes that the NIH should apportion research funds proportional to the US burden of disease.

entry.Resolution:
Information:  In American politics, Democratic Party superdelegates include distinguished party leaders, and elected officials, including all Democratic members of the House and Senate and sitting Democratic governors. Democratic superdelegates are free to support any candidate for the nomination. This contrasts with convention "pledged" delegates who are selected based on the party primaries and caucuses in each U.S. state, in which voters choose among candidates for the party's presidential nomination. Because they are free to support anyone they want, superdelegates could potentially swing the results to nominate a presidential candidate who did not receive the majority of votes during the primaries.
This House would abolish superdelegates.
entry.Name: Osterweis
entry.Topic Committee: Yale Debate Association

entry.Resolution:
THW bring back the Fairness Doctrine.
The Fairness Doctrine was a FCC (Federal Communications Commission) rule which stated broadcasters (such as TV or radio stations) had to cover controversial topics which were important to Americans. Also, broadcasters had to report on both sides of these controversial issues equally. Finally, the rule said anyone attacked on TV or radio had to be given an opportunity to respond to the attack on air.

entry.Resolution:
In 1954 the United States Supreme Court ruled that racial segregation in public schools was unconstitutional, ending segregationist practices that had persisted in parts of the U.S., including Arkansas, since the end of the Civil War.  The Governor of Arkansas threatened to defy this decision using the National Guard and State law enforcement, leading to a stand-off with the Federal Government in which President Eisenhower promised Marine guards to any student agreeing to forcibly integrate the all-white Little Rock Central High School for the 1957-58 school year.  As a Black parent living in Little Rock, Arkansas, in 1957 with no supernatural knowledge of the outcome,
THBT you should volunteer your child to forcibly integrate the high school.
entry.Name: Osterweis

tournaments.Note: The rules at Whitman are very different than what we are used to:On POIs:Each speaker MUST take at least one question during his/her constructive speech AND the question is not timed.Questions may not be asked during the first and last 30 seconds of the constructive speeches.Students may ask questions during the 1 minute preparation time periods.Speech times:Prime Minister Constructive: 3 min.1 minute preparation/cross-examinationLeader of Opposition Constructive: 4 min.1 minute preparation/cross-examinationMember of Government Constructive 4 min.1 minute preparation/cross-examinationMember of Opposition Constructive 4 min.Leader of Opposition Rebuttal 3 min.1 minute preparation/cross-examinationPrime Minister Rebuttal 4 min.The topics are already set
